elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement without Vendor consent to an Affiliate.
elements.evidence: Section 15.6 expressly permits PB to assign or transfer the Agreement in its entirety to any Affiliate without SFJ's consent.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement without Vendor consent to a successor in connection with a merger.
elements.evidence: The PB-only carve-out permits assignment to a successor in connection with a transfer of the relevant business or assets, expressly including by merger.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement without Vendor consent to a successor in connection with an acquisition.
elements.evidence: The PB-only successor carve-out covers sale of stock, sale of assets, or otherwise, which operatively encompasses an acquisition of the relevant business.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement without Vendor consent to a successor in connection with a sale of all or substantially all assets.
elements.evidence: The PB-only carve-out expressly covers a successor in connection with a sale or transfer of all or substantially all business or assets to which the Agreement relates.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign the Agreement without Customer's prior written consent.
elements.evidence: SFJ has no Affiliate or successor carve-out and therefore remains subject to PB's prior written consent for assignments and transfers.

elements.element: For Vendor assignments that are not prohibited competitor assignments, Customer's consent may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Although the general consent standard is not to be unreasonably withheld, the notwithstanding clause allows PB to withhold consent in its sole discretion for every entity whose primary business is pharmaceutical or biotechnology development or commercialization. That category is not limited to Customer competitors and therefore can include otherwise permitted non-competitor assignments.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign the Agreement to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: The clause is not an absolute prohibition: it permits transfer to the specified pharmaceutical or biotechnology entities if PB consents. It also does not define the prohibited entities by reference to competition with PB.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate the Agreement because of Customer's change of control.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2.6 expressly states that SFJ has no right to terminate the Agreement as a result of a Change of Control of PB.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement to a successor without Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: The PB-only carve-out permits assignment to a successor in connection with the specified merger, stock-sale, asset-sale, and similar transactions.

elements.element: Customer must give Vendor written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: Section 15.6 contains no written-notice requirement for a successor assignment. The separate notice of a definitive agreement for a PB Change of Control is not an assignment notice and does not demonstrably cover every successor assignment.

elements.element: Vendor may assign the Agreement to a successor without Customer consent.
elements.evidence: The successor carve-out is limited to PB. SFJ therefore requires PB's consent even for an assignment to SFJ's successor.

elements.element: Vendor must give Customer written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: No written-notice mechanism is provided for an SFJ successor assignment; instead, PB's prior consent is required.

elements.element: Customer assignments other than assignments to a successor require Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: PB may also assign without consent to any Affiliate, including an Affiliate that is not a successor.

elements.element: Vendor may not unreasonably withhold consent to Customer assignments requiring consent.
elements.evidence: For PB assignments outside its Affiliate and successor carve-outs, the general clause requires SFJ's prior written consent and states that consent may not be unreasonably withheld.

elements.element: Vendor assignments other than assignments to a successor require Customer consent.
elements.evidence: SFJ has no successor or Affiliate carve-out, and both the general rule and the pharmaceutical/biotechnology transferee provision require PB's consent.

elements.element: Customer may not unreasonably withhold consent to Vendor assignments requiring consent.
elements.evidence: PB may withhold consent in its sole discretion where the proposed SFJ transferee's primary business is pharmaceutical or biotechnology development or commercialization.

result.reason: The redline correctly gives PB Affiliate and successor assignment freedom, removes SFJ's change-of-control termination right, and generally subjects SFJ assignments to PB consent. It nevertheless misses the preferred absolute competitor prohibition because the operative language permits the transfer with PB's consent and uses an overbroad industry-based category rather than a Customer-competitor standard. It also fails the fallback because successor rights are not mutual, no comprehensive written-notice requirement is included, PB retains a non-successor Affiliate carve-out, and PB may withhold consent in its sole discretion for a category of SFJ assignments. The draft also ends the PB carve-out with a dangling “and,” reducing drafting quality. The changes otherwise preserve the commercial consequences of removing the change-of-control termination right.
